entry.title: Dengue · Europe: Italy: 68 local dengue cases in 5 outbreaks; France unchanged at 6
entry.summary: The ISS counts 346 confirmed dengue cases from 1 January to 6 October; 68 were locally acquired, linked to 5 outbreaks plus 1 case not linked to the others, and there were no deaths. One of 29 chikungunya cases was locally acquired. Santé publique France's 7 October bulletin (data to 5 October) still counts 4 local dengue episodes with 6 cases, and 20 local chikungunya episodes with 146 cases.
entry.content:
The ISS counts 346 confirmed dengue cases from 1 January to 6 October; 68 were locally acquired, linked to 5 outbreaks plus 1 case not linked to the others, and there were no deaths. One of 29 chikungunya cases was locally acquired. Santé publique France's 7 October bulletin (data to 5 October) still counts 4 local dengue episodes with 6 cases, and 20 local chikungunya episodes with 146 cases.

Sources: Quotidiano Sanità, AgenSIR, Santé publique France bulletin, 7 Oct

entry.title: Plague · Russia: Governor says quarantine lifted and monitoring of all contacts complete
entry.summary: Irkutsk Governor Igor Kobzev said in a video address on 8 October that the quarantine at Shelekhov District Hospital has been lifted, about a week after the worker's death. Regional media report that Rospotrebnadzor said the full set of preventive measures was completed on 8 October, with medical monitoring finished for all contacts, no health changes linked to infectious disease, and nearly 5,000 laboratory tests that found no dangerous pathogenic microorganisms. Officially the cause of death remains "pneumonia of unknown etiology". WHO has not yet said whether it has received the pathogen details it asked for.
entry.content:
Irkutsk Governor Igor Kobzev said in a video address on 8 October that the quarantine at Shelekhov District Hospital has been lifted, about a week after the worker's death. Regional media report that Rospotrebnadzor said the full set of preventive measures was completed on 8 October, with medical monitoring finished for all contacts, no health changes linked to infectious disease, and nearly 5,000 laboratory tests that found no dangerous pathogenic microorganisms. Officially the cause of death remains "pneumonia of unknown etiology". WHO has not yet said whether it has received the pathogen details it asked for.

Sources: IrCity, EANews, Kyiv Independent, Mediazona, The Moscow Times (Russian service)

entry.title: Measles · US: Pennsylvania: 1,078 cases in 41 counties
entry.summary: The state health department's Wednesday update counts 1,078 confirmed cases, 207 hospitalisations and 5 measles-associated deaths. Lancaster County has 401 cases and Mifflin County 153. About 40 of the 74 cases added since 5 October were older infections only recently confirmed, and the department said the update does not reflect a current surge in new infections.

entry.title: Plague · Russia: WHO asks Russia for the pathogen, test results and contact details
entry.summary: WHO Director-General Tedros said WHO does not yet have the full picture and cannot conduct a full risk assessment. WHO has asked Russia about the pathogen behind the pneumonia, the lab tests, the contacts and their health, and about media reports of a second employee with pneumonia of undetermined cause. Those reports have not been confirmed by local officials. WHO's initial assessment stands: moderate to low for Irkutsk, low for Russia, very low for Europe. WHO said it has seen no evidence of plague spreading.
entry.content:
WHO Director-General Tedros said WHO does not yet have the full picture and cannot conduct a full risk assessment. Those reports have not been confirmed by local officials. WHO's initial assessment stands: moderate to low for Irkutsk, low for Russia, very low for Europe. WHO said it has seen no evidence of plague spreading.

Sources: CNN, The Washington Times

entry.title: Plague · Russia: Rospotrebnadzor: monitoring complete for over 90% of contacts
entry.summary: Russia's consumer safety watchdog said that as of 7 October medical monitoring had been completed for more than 90% of the people who had contact with the worker. It said no health changes linked to infectious disease were detected and that nearly 5,000 laboratory tests found no dangerous pathogenic microorganisms. It said there is no risk to residents of Irkutsk and the region. The cause of death remains officially "pneumonia of unknown etiology".
entry.content:
Russia's consumer safety watchdog said that as of 7 October medical monitoring had been completed for more than 90% of the people who had contact with the worker. It said no health changes linked to infectious disease were detected and that nearly 5,000 laboratory tests found no dangerous pathogenic microorganisms. It said there is no risk to residents of Irkutsk and the region. The cause of death remains officially "pneumonia of unknown etiology".

Sources: CNN, Fontanka

entry.title: Plague · Russia: Kremlin calls most media reports false; second-case reports unconfirmed
entry.summary: Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said "the vast majority" of media reporting on the situation is false information and urged people to rely on Rospotrebnadzor's statements. Media have reported a second institute employee with pneumonia, and some outlets a second death; Russian officials have confirmed neither. WHO has asked Russia to clarify the reports.
entry.content:

Sources: Al Jazeera, Euronews

entry.title: Plague · Russia: US asks Russia for more information; Putin call not yet arranged
entry.summary: A State Department spokesperson said the US has officially requested additional information from the Russian government. President Trump has said he plans to speak with President Putin about the case. The Kremlin said on 7 October that no call had been arranged yet but that it was open to one.

entry.title: Plague · Russia: No plague found in contacts tested so far
entry.summary: Russian officials say plague has not been detected among close contacts, with about 60% of the group tested. Testing found 2 Covid-19 and 2 rhinovirus cases and no other dangerous pathogens.
entry.content:
Russian officials say plague has not been detected among close contacts, with about 60% of the group tested. Testing found 2 Covid-19 and 2 rhinovirus cases and no other dangerous pathogens.

entry.title: Plague · Russia: Russia tells WHO no plague found in contacts; WHO rates the risk
entry.summary: Russian authorities told WHO that no dangerous pathogens were found in any contact tested and none have symptoms. WHO's first risk assessment: moderate to low for Irkutsk, low for Russia, very low for Europe. Earlier the same day WHO had said it was still waiting for a formal reply.
entry.content:
Russian authorities told WHO that no dangerous pathogens were found in any contact tested and none have symptoms. WHO's first risk assessment: moderate to low for Irkutsk, low for Russia, very low for Europe. Earlier the same day WHO had said it was still waiting for a formal reply.

Sources: UN News, NBC News, PBS NewsHour

entry.title: Mpox · Africa & world: CDC: more than 80 clade I cases in at least 22 states
entry.summary: CDC's updated count is more than 80 laboratory-confirmed clade I cases in at least 22 states since November 2024, up from more than 60 in at least 20 states on 25 September. CDC says cases with presumed domestic transmission have been reported in more than 10 jurisdictions and rates the risk to most people as low.
entry.content:
CDC's updated count is more than 80 laboratory-confirmed clade I cases in at least 22 states since November 2024, up from more than 60 in at least 20 states on 25 September. CDC says cases with presumed domestic transmission have been reported in more than 10 jurisdictions and rates the risk to most people as low.

Sources: CDC: current situation, Medscape

entry.title: Cholera · Global: ECDC: 249,136 cases worldwide this year
entry.summary: ECDC's monthly overview counts 249,136 cases, including 1,970 deaths, from 1 January to 28 September, against 436,268 cases and 4,449 deaths at the same point in 2025. In the month to 28 September it recorded 46,153 new cases and 140 deaths; Afghanistan (34,378), DR Congo (8,505) and Yemen (1,885) reported the most cases. ECDC's totals are a separate count from the WHO figures above.

CDC rates the risk to most people as low.
